name: propetl
description: Convert property-management spreadsheets into Yardi Voyager 7S import files and draft schema-verified ySQL.

interface.longDescription:
PropETL turns the property-management exports you already have into Yardi-ready Voyager 7S import files: hand it an Excel or CSV of units, leases, tenants, charges or residents and it profiles every sheet, maps your columns to Yardi fields, validates the data against 5,204 Yardi import rules, and returns an import-ready template plus a plain-English explanation of anything that will be rejected.

It also answers Yardi data questions as schema-verified ySQL and report scripts - rent rolls, lease expiries, delinquency and aging, GL balance checks - drafted against a knowledge base of 9,793 standard Voyager tables, 6,572 field definitions and proven query patterns. Every table, column and coded value is looked up in the knowledge base before it is used; queries are delivered ready to run in ySQL.

For go-lives, PropETL sequences the full ETL upload chronology for new migrations or adding a property to an existing system (commercial/retail and residential).

Scope: Yardi Voyager 7S only. Access requires connecting your PropETL account.
capabilities: Convert Excel/CSV into Yardi import templates
Validate and explain Yardi import data
Draft schema-verified ySQL queries and reports
defaultPrompt: Convert this Excel into a Yardi units import template
Write a ySQL rent roll query as of month end
What order should I upload Yardi ETL files for a new commercial property?

positive.description: KB table lookup for lease tables
positive.prompt: Which Yardi Voyager tables hold lease data?
positive.expected_behavior: Searches the knowledge base and returns lease tables that exist in it (e.g. Lease_History, BIResLease, CommPropLeaseType), then column-level detail for one of them via get_yardi_table_schema. Never names a table outside the knowledge base.

positive.description: FK join path between two Voyager tables
positive.prompt: How do I join PMUSER to PROPERTY in a ySQL query?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the 2-hop path PMUSER.HMY = Billpay_EmailNotificationRequests.hUser, then .hProperty = PROPERTY.HMY, with a JOIN snippet, and flags when an edge is inferred from H-prefix naming rather than a confirmed FK.

positive.description: Rent-roll query from the proven pattern library
positive.prompt: Write me a ySQL rent roll query as of end of month.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the rent_roll pattern (Leasing; TENANT, UNIT, PROPERTY, CAMRULE, CHARGTYP) adapted to the request, lists the placeholders (property code, as-of date) with an example value each, and grounds column names via get_yardi_table_schema. If a pattern name is not in the library the tool lists the available names so the right one is picked.

positive.prompt: What order do I upload Yardi ETL files when migrating a new commercial retail property?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the commercial_retail new-migration chronology: 36 ordered steps starting with Comm_Owners, each with its import_type and dependency, plus the note that it is best-practice guidance.

positive.prompt: What fields does the Yardi Units import require?
positive.expected_behavior: Resolves the Units module to CommUnits and returns its 49 field definitions with data type, max length and required flags; the 8 mandatory fields are Property_Code, Unit_Code, Rental_Type, Country, Ext_Ref_Unit_Id, Ref_Property_Id, Ref_Building_Id and Ref_Floor_Id.

negative.prompt: Run this query against my Yardi database and show me the rows.
Email all tenants about the rent increase.
Import this MRI lease report into Yardi Breeze.

review.commerce_description: The plugin does not sell products or process payments inside the chat; access is through a connected PropETL account.

publication.release_notes: 1.0.2 - review test cases re-verified against the live MCP endpoint and re-pointed where a prompt did not exercise a working tool path (lease-table lookup replaces the CAM-escalation phrasing, rent-roll case names the real pattern, join and field-requirement expectations cite verified output). Server instructions trimmed to the schema-grounding protocol: removed the in-instructions sales prompt and the instruction to suppress caveats; the server now states plainly that it drafts SQL and does not execute queries.
